properties.description:
The `capture-session` skill, shipped 2026-08-12 as the FIRST STEP settled in dec:idea-a-capture-session-skill-the-user-types. Served like every other skill (19 in the catalogue) and invocable at any point in a session, not only at the end.

WHAT IT IS, PRECISELY: a TRIGGER, not a memory. cap:session-memory stays PLANNED and this does not realize it — the connective tissue still has no node type of its own, which the skill states as one of its own limits rather than papering over.

THE TWO PROBLEMS IT HAD TO SOLVE, both left open by the brainstorm node:
  1. WHO JUDGES IMPORTANCE. Not solved by judgement — solved by removing the judgement. The skill gives six concrete tests (a reason that exists nowhere else / somebody measured something / the user corrected you / something was tried and abandoned / a finding arrived sideways / the user stated a rule in passing) under one question: would a session six weeks from now redo this work because nobody wrote it down?
  2. NO HOME FOR THE TISSUE. Routed to nearest neighbours, explicitly and reversibly: reasoning into its Decision, a road not taken into that same Decision's text, a measurement to a TemporalFact, a project change to a ChangeEvent, a lesson to a DesignEpoch, a stated rule to a DesignRule, new intent OUT to capture-intent.

HONEST STANDING: req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session is ACCEPTED, says the user must never be the trigger, and is NOT met by this. The skill says so in its own text so a reader cannot mistake shipped for satisfied.

═══ FIRST DOGFOOD, 2026-08-12, WITHIN THE HOUR — AND IT FOUND A HOLE IN ITS OWN ROUTING TABLE ═══

Anthony ran the skill to close the session it was built in ("can we try our new skill out?"). It worked, and the most useful output was a defect in itself.

🛑 THE ROUTING TABLE HAS NO ROW FOR A FACT ABOUT THE USER. Test 3 ("did the user correct you?") and test 6 ("did the user state a rule in passing?") both fired on the same correction from earlier in the session: Anthony was referred to in the THIRD PERSON in a reply addressed TO HIM ("the owner reports…"). The rule that came out of it — SECOND PERSON when speaking to the user, THIRD PERSON in graph node text, because a node is a durable record for later readers who need a name — is exactly what test 6 is for. But the table's only offer is DesignRule, and that is wrong: this is not a rule about reflow2's design, it is a fact about a person. Writing it as a DesignRule would put a user preference into the design vocabulary where every future reader has to route around it.

⇒ THE CORRECT HOME WAS THE AGENT'S OWN MEMORY, NOT THE GRAPH, and the skill does not say so. The gap is narrow and real: the six tests are written to catch things about the PERSON as readily as things about the DESIGN, while the routing table below them only knows how to place design content. An agent following the skill literally would either drop the finding or mis-file it.

FIX DIRECTION (not applied — recorded so the next reader does not re-derive it): the routing table needs a row for "a fact about the user, or how they want to be worked with" pointing OUT of the graph, the same way "new intent" already points out to capture-intent. The skill already has the shape for this; it is one row.

📌 WHAT THE SKILL GOT RIGHT ON ITS FIRST RUN, worth recording because it is the failure mode it was written against: it DECLINED to capture. A drifted prose count in getting-started/README.md ("the 15 workflows" while the kit served 18) was noticed, fixed in the same commit, and deliberately NOT given a node — a later session would have re-fixed it in two minutes, so nothing would have been lost. And the session's MCP outage was routed to an EXISTING fact as an addendum rather than a fifth near-duplicate node. Two of the four candidates that came up were correctly refused.

⚠️ CAVEAT ON THIS RUN'S EVIDENCE, per the skill's own instruction to say what could not be verified: the session was COMPACTED, so its earlier hours survive only as a summary. Everything above is from the post-compaction stretch, which was directly observed.
properties.name: A user-typed trigger for capturing what only the session holds
